answer: Each new agent must lock a non-transferable stake to a single-use hardware attestation, creating an identity relic that cannot be cloned across accounts. Subsequent actions require endorsements from independently sampled peers; those signatures ripple through at least three disjoint clusters before the stake gains voting weight. A rotating garden of established attestors then audits the endorsement graph for near-duplicate behavioral fingerprints. Detected multi-account clusters are slashed and evicted, so buying influence costs more than manufacturing identities can return.
